Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the chase. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Georgia Voll and Beth Mooney open up for the Aussies. Shawnisha Hector has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
... The Run Chase ...

Clinical Australia on target - It was a beautifully disciplined bowling display from the Australians, who never let the pressure slip. Lucy Hamilton and Ashleigh Gardner led the charge with an excellent spell, picking up two crucial wickets each. They received fantastic support from the rest of the unit, with Sophie Molineux, Nicola Carey, Ellyse Perry, Kim Garth and Georgia Wareham picking up one wicket apiece. Australia will be very happy with this effort as they prepare to chase down 132 for the win.

Dottin fought a lone battle - The only real resistance came from Deandra Dottin, who showed incredible grit out in the middle. She played a magnificent knock of 46, standing tall while wickets tumbled around her. Just when she looked set to take her team to a safer position, she suffered an unlucky dismissal. With no other batters stepping up to score big, the West Indies innings completely fizzled out after her departure.

Aussie bowlers restrict the Windies - Australia Women are firmly in the driver's seat after a clinical performance with the ball. The West Indies Women found it tough to build any real momentum right from the start. Every time a decent partnership looked like it was brewing, the Australian bowlers struck back quickly to break it. The Windies just couldn't get going and finished with a below-par total of 131 runs, getting bowled out.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin! The two umpires are walking out to the middle now, followed by the Australia Women players. They spread out to take up their respective field positions. Qiana Joseph and Hayley Matthews are the two openers for West Indies Women. Kim Garth has the new ball in her hand and is ready to go. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Charles Dagnall is pitchside. He says that there is a bit of a turn here in the pitch, as we saw in the game earlier between India Women and England Women. Mentions that the ball grips a bit, but overall, it's a high-scoring venue. Ends by saying that the par score here is around 170-180, so if you bat first, you need to score at least around 170 runs.

The skipper of Australia Women - Sophie Molineux says that she is fine with bowling first, although they would have batted first as well. Adds that the team is in good spirits and are looking to put on another good performance. Sophie mentions that there are no injuries in the group, except for Phoebe Litchfield, who has niggle, but she reckons that it is not serious. Ends by saying that she saw the ball turn a bit in the last game here and hopes that she can use that to her advantage.

The captain of West Indies Women - Hayley Matthews says that the same track is being used and the conditions are good, so they'll be batting first. Hayley mentions that they are looking to minor out any combinations if left. Ends by saying that they will be utilising all 15 players.

Australia Women - Beth Mooney (WK), Georgia Voll, Ellyse Perry, Ashleigh Gardner, Grace Harris, Annabel Sutherland, Tahlia McGrath, Phoebe Litchfield, Kim Garth, Alana King, Lucy Hamilton, Sophie Molineux (C), Megan Schutt, Georgia Wareham, Nicola Carey, Tahlia Wilson.

West Indies Women - Hayley Matthews (C), Deandra Dottin, Shemaine Campbelle (WK), Qiana Joseph, Jahzara Claxton, Aaliyah Alleyne, Chinelle Henry, Jannillea Glasgow, Zaida James, Shawnisha Hector, Afy Fletcher, Mandy Mangru, Ashmini Munisar, Karishma Ramharack, Stafanie Taylor.
TOSS - ​West Indies Women have won the toss and they will be batting first.

Fitness first - While both camps are thoroughly enjoying their time out in the middle, the overriding priority for this final warm-up fixture is navigating the match completely injury-free. The harsh reality of pre-tournament casualties was felt just yesterday when the Netherlands' Isabel van der Woning suffered a suspected hamstring injury against Sri Lanka, a devastating blow that could cut short her World Cup dream. Consequently, while this clash will undoubtedly be played in high spirits and with intense competitive drive, every athlete on the field will be hyper-focused on coming out of the contest fully fit and ready for the official group stages.

England edge India in warm-up thriller - Match 11 has ended in a victory for the host nation. It was all going England's way until India's wicketkeeper, Richa Ghosh, decided to take matters into her own hands and turn the match on its head. Launching a spectacular and well-calculated counter-attack, Ghosh began sighting the ball perfectly, smashing boundaries at will to bring the Asian side within touching distance of an improbable victory. With India needing just 6 runs from the final 3 deliveries, the match hung in the balance. However, England’s Linsey Smith held her nerve under immense pressure, dismissing the dangerous Ghosh before cleaning up the final Indian batter on the very next ball to seal a dramatic five-run victory.

England closing in on victory against India - Tournament hosts England Women are on the brink of securing victory over India Women at Sophia Gardens in the first game of this double header. Chasing a formidable target of 172, India's batting lineup crumbled under relentless pressure, leaving them needing an improbable 38 runs from the final two overs with just two wickets in hand. Barring a miraculous Richa Ghosh blitz, England's disciplined bowling unit is set to wrap up the tail and carry immense winning momentum straight into the tournament opener. All you need to do is switch tabs to get updates and analysis from that contest as we continue to build here.

Fine-tuning the combinations for glory - This final warm-up fixture provides both teams with a priceless opportunity to solidify their best playing XIs and build psychological momentum. Captains and coaches will utilize the flexible warm-up rules to experiment with different bowling match-ups, test their death-overs execution, and solidify their ideal batting positions under true match pressure. Stepping onto the field one last time before the official tournament begins, a victory here will be crucial. Securing a win not only clears up tactical doubts but also infuses the squad with a vital surge of winning momentum heading directly into the fiercely contested group stages of the ICC Women's T20 World Cup. Toss and team news to follow...

Australia's quest to maintain dominance - Australia Women enter this match, and the tournament proper, as the undisputed team to beat. Their overwhelming dominance in women's cricket is anchored by an incredibly deep roster full of elite all-rounders and seasoned pressure-performers. With the legendary Ellyse Perry firing and a relentless bowling attack led by Megan Schutt, the Aussies possess unparalleled balance across all departments. Despite their clinical aura, the management will be looking to iron out minor chinks in their armor, specifically ensuring that their star-studded batting lineup remains ruthless against high-quality spin and avoids any middle-order complacency when chasing targets.

Powerhouse potential of West Indies - West Indies Women possess a lineup packed with destructive power hitters and experienced match-winners who can dismantle any bowling attack on their day. Boasting unmatched athletic capability, their primary strength lies in an explosive top order featuring veteran stars like Deandra Dottin and Chinelle Henry, who looked sharp with a 49-run knock against India. However, to mount a serious title challenge in the main tournament, the Caribbean side desperately needs to address their bowling consistency and situational execution. After straying in line and leaking runs during the Powerplay against India, the bowlers must find a way to maintain discipline, stifle runs in the middle overs, and establish a well-balanced formula before the real stakes begin.

The final countdown in Cardiff - Welcome to all cricket fans to Sophia Gardens in Cardiff, where the final preparations for the ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026 reach an exciting climax. Match 12 is the very last warm-up contest before the main tournament officially gets underway. Both teams have experienced contrasting fortunes in their initial outings. Australia Women kicked off their campaign with a convincing five-wicket victory over England, while West Indies Women suffered a 26-run defeat to India. With the global showpiece starting right after this clash, this fixture serves as the ultimate audition for both camps to fine-tune their strategies and adjust to local playing conditions.
